why: From 1 July 2027, UAE businesses with annual revenue under AED 50 million must issue and receive business invoices as e-invoices. Larger businesses start on 1 January 2027.
These businesses must appoint an e-invoicing provider accredited by the Ministry of Finance by 31 March 2027.
For invoices to other businesses, a PDF or Word file will no longer count. The invoice must be a structured e-invoice sent through an accredited provider.
Businesses that miss the deadline face fines of AED 5,000 a month (up to AED 50,000 in any 12 months), plus AED 100 for each invoice not issued as an e-invoice (up to AED 5,000 a month).
why_close: Do not wait for the deadline. Buy today and we start your setup.
why_source: Source: UAE Ministry of Finance decisions on the e-invoicing system, checked 24 November 2026.
